# Content

## Portfolio Project Title

GoDaddy: Native Shipping Labels Integration

## Subtitle

Improving the order fulfillment process for Power Sellers by natively integrating ShipEngine into the GoDaddy Commerce ecosystem.

## The Problem Space

Store owners were losing valuable time searching externally for the best shipping label rates, taking their focus away from business growth. GoDaddy's existing multi-carrier solution, Shippo, suffered from incredibly low adoption (only 11.3% of 44,000 monthly active sellers used it) due to complexity and lack of platform trust.

## Hypothesis

By natively integrating shipping label purchases and providing a highly guided setup flow, we could save "Power Sellers" (merchants generating $100K+ in annual volume) significant time and money without forcing them to leave the GoDaddy platform.

## Constraint

The new solution required integrating a third-party partner API (ShipEngine). This meant users had to navigate a lengthy setup process: agreeing to terms, adding payment info, and funding their account. This carried a high risk of user fatigue and information overload.

## Design Iteration & Trade-offs (The Messy Middle)

To solve the complex onboarding and layout constraints, I explored multiple UI paths:

* Layout tradeoffs: For the core "Buy Shipping Label" page, I drafted 2-column, 3-column, and step-by-step layout variations. After multiple architectural reviews, we determined the 2-column layout was the most viable and readable solution for the MVP.  
* View & Print: Initially, "View" and "Print" were treated as separate UI actions, which created awkward empty spaces in the layout. We pivoted to a cleaner, 3 side by side card layout during a later sprint to consolidate these post-purchase actions.

During usability testing with the GoDaddy Customer Council, we uncovered a critical insight: Users did not trust the unbranded ShipEngine setup screens (“I don't see any GoDaddy logo... can I trust them?”). This immediate feedback led us to inject GoDaddy branding directly into the third-party ShipEngine flow to bridge the trust gap before final handoff.

## Solution

I designed a structured, end to end fulfillment flow utilizing GoDaddy's "DeepSee" design system and all the gathered data from previous iterations and usability tests.

The journey begins seamlessly on the Order Details page with a promotional modal. To prevent UI annoyance, if a user selects "Maybe Later," the modal is programmed with a snooze logic and will not reappear until a set period has passed. Users are then routed through an educational Shipping Settings page before entering the simplified ShipEngine setup. Once they are done with that, they are redirected to a clean, 2 column interface to calculate rates, pick a label, and purchase the label. After purchase, they can view and print their label, customize the packing slip, and refund the label if needed.

## Edge Cases Considered

* **API Validation Gates:** The interface requires users to enter physical package dimensions and validate the "Ship To" address before the ShipEngine API is allowed to return available shipping rates, preventing excessive API calls and inaccurate pricing.  
* **Fatigue Mitigation**: Recognizing the high friction of a multi-step third-party onboarding process, the flow is explicitly designed to allow users to skip the setup of specific carriers and complete them at a later time.

## Outcomes

The integration resulted in 6,722 users actively utilizing the feature within its first three months, successfully generating 7,521 purchased shipping labels.

The feature achieved immediate traction, with 2,000 GoDaddy Commerce users adopting the integration right at launch, which earned our team a shout-out in a company All-Hands meeting.

## Retrospective

Integrating third-party tools into a native enterprise ecosystem is a delicate balance of trust and usability. User testing proved that keeping merchants within their home ecosystem was highly valued ("I wouldn't trust my shipping to other companies").

The success of this project reinforced that maintaining brand presence is critical for feature adoption and user confidence.

I’m glad I was able to update the UI at a later point thanks to the Antares design system. There was also a future enhancement planned but that’s a story for another day.
